sections.content: You know *porque* and *por eso* from A2 Unit 5 and *además* from A2 Unit 28. New here: *ya que* (“since”, a reason the listener already knows) and *en cambio* (“by contrast”). Use them to link claims to reasons, consequences and opposing ideas.

items.spanish: Apoyo la medida porque podría reducir el problema a largo plazo.
items.english: I support the measure because it could reduce the problem in the long term.

items.spanish: La propuesta es cara; por eso, necesitamos otra opción.
items.english: The proposal is expensive; that is why we need another option.

items.spanish: Apoyo la medida ya que podría reducir el problema y mejorar la situación.
items.english: I support the measure since it could reduce the problem and improve the situation.

items.spanish: Además, existe evidencia que apoya esta postura.
items.english: Furthermore, there is evidence that supports this position.

items.spanish: En cambio, la segunda propuesta sería más sencilla y tendría menos costes.
items.english: By contrast, the second proposal would be simpler and would have fewer costs.

sections.content: Remember: *en cambio* signals contrast (“on the other hand”), so it goes with an opposing idea, not with a result. For a result use *por eso*.
